# Supported workloads

Which multi-node engine shapes nvsnap captures and restores today, and which it refuses. A refused instance is not
an error: it runs normally and starts cold, and the agent logs why. Each row gives the agent log line to search for.

<!-- toc: generated by scripts/docs/docs-toc.py; edit the headings, not this list -->
**Contents**

- [Not supported yet](#not-supported-yet)
- [Restores that are refused](#restores-that-are-refused)
<!-- /toc -->

## Not supported yet

| Workload shape | What nvsnap does | Agent log | Decided in |
|---|---|---|---|
| A namespace with 2 or more Grove scaling group replicas (multi-replica Dynamo; prefill and decode groups count) | Captures and restores none of them: the replicas share their etcd, NATS and frontend, and a group capture or restore of one would stop or restore what the others use | `CRIU group capture: skipped; the instance starts from the caches` with `reason="the namespace runs N Grove scaling group replicas, which share their companions ..."` | `sharedCompanionsReason`, `internal/agent/grove_replicas.go` |
| A worker whose configuration names its own instance, such as Dynamo's Kubernetes discovery (`GROVE_HEADLESS_SERVICE`) with the TCP request plane | Does not capture it: a restored process keeps that configuration and would run as the old instance | `CRIU group capture: skipped; the pod names its own instance in its configuration ...` or `... a rank names its own instance in its configuration` | `identityBlocksCapture`, called from `considerGroupCapture` and `captureGroup` in `internal/agent/criu_group.go` |
| A worker that holds RDMA devices: NCCL over InfiniBand, ModelExpress (NIXL/UCX weight transfer), NIXL KV transfer | The capture preflight refuses it when its host checks find the devices: a checkpoint cannot save RDMA state. Exception: a ModelExpress process on a node whose GPU tool has `mx-pause` is only noted, since the capture has ModelExpress release its RDMA right before the suspend; if any RDMA device is still held then, `mx-pause` fails and the capture ends before the instance is stopped. If a member's host checks cannot run, the preflight records a warning (`host checks did not run: ...`) that does not block the capture; RDMA devices that `mx-pause` does not release then fail the dump | `CRIU group capture preflight: process <pid> (<comm>) holds RDMA devices <devices>: a checkpoint cannot save RDMA state (checkpoint-restore/criu#267) ...` (search for `holds RDMA devices`), then `CRIU group capture: skipped; the preflight found what would fail it` | `rdmaFindings`, `processFindings` and `capturePreflight` (host-check warning), `internal/agent/capture_preflight.go`; `releasedByMXPause` and `pauseModelExpress`, `internal/agent/gpushare_mx.go` |
| Prefill/decode disaggregation | Refused by both rows above (several groups, and NIXL's RDMA). The shared-companions check runs first (`sharedCompanionsBlockCapture`, before `capturePreflight` in `captureGroup`), so only its refusal is logged | the shared-companions line above; not the RDMA one | `captureGroup`, `internal/agent/criu_group.go` |
| A Dynamo rank connected to no etcd or NATS in its namespace | Does not capture it: there is nothing to capture with it | `CRIU group capture: skipped; a Dynamo rank is connected to no etcd or NATS of its namespace to capture with it` | `captureGroup`, `internal/agent/criu_group.go` |

Releasing RDMA around a capture is in review in #3522: an RDMA verbs library that releases and re-creates NCCL's RDMA
state, pause and resume for ModelExpress and NIXL, and their pause checks with NCCL over InfiniBand. Until it merges,
this page describes `main`. Even with them, ModelExpress and NIXL KV transfer in one process
stay unsupported: each pause trips on the other's RDMA.

## Restores that are refused

A restore is refused, and the pod starts cold, when the new pod's process configuration (command, args, env) differs
from the checkpoint's: the restored process would keep the old one. The webhook logs the first difference, for example
`changed="main: env DYN_NAMESPACE_WORKER_SUFFIX"`, with one of these lines:

- a group member: `CRIU group restore: the pod's process configuration differs from its checkpoint's, which the
  restored process would keep; cold start` (`criuGroupRestorePatches`, `internal/webhook/criu_group.go`)
- a single pod: `CRIU restore: the pod's process configuration differs from its checkpoint's, which the restored
  process would keep; cold start` (`internal/webhook/criu_restore.go`)

The configuration is recorded by `ProcessConfig` and compared by `ProcessConfigChanges`
(`internal/webhook/process_config.go`). A checkpoint taken before the configuration was recorded has no record to
compare: `ProcessConfigChanges` returns no difference for an empty record, so such a checkpoint is restored even when
the pod's command, args or env changed.

Known gap: the instance that starts cold after such a refusal is not captured again, because the configuration's
record already says `complete` (`CRIU group capture: skipped; the configuration's record says it is captured, being
captured, or out of attempts`; `captureGroup` and `groupRecaptures` in `internal/agent/criu_group.go`). A function that NVCF redeploys with a new
`DYN_NAMESPACE_WORKER_SUFFIX` therefore stops restoring until that record is removed.
